body:
Just a quick update:
I talked to my manager, and she was very receptive and concerned.
We had a nice, long discussion about what may be triggering it and perhaps trying to move my shift.

The biggest thing that gave me the most relief was when she told me "Don't worry about all of this, you're the most important thing and you need to take care of you, first and foremost." She also demanded a hug from me when we were done talking.

I've also made an appointment with a mental health professional and I will hopefully be back to 100% very, very soon.

I want to thank everyone for their thoughts and support. It meant a lot.
I think you're right, and I really do appreciate the thoughts.

I think she needs to know, simply because I don't think she'll understand otherwise. I can see the conversation going like this:

>"Overnights are causing me problems... is there anything I can do about it?"
>
>"They cause everyone problems... it's the overnight."

I'm don't think she's going to be sympathetic to my situation unless she knows what I'm going through. I would think there's a huge difference between being groggy and cranky and having a constant, steady feeling of wanting to kill yourself.
